hypotheses.justification: `ModularCurve.smoothedFundamental Γ T z` is a `finsum` over `SL(2,ℤ) ⧸ Γ` (Definitions/Def_ModularCurve_SmoothedFundamental.lean, line 170). That definition needs no finiteness; with infinite index the finsum may take the junk value 0, which only shrinks the support. The current proof uses FiniteIndex only through `carrier`/`isCompact_carrierH`/`mem_carrier_of_ne_zero`, i.e. through the Fintype instance on the quotient. Alternative proof without it: let S = {δ : SL(2,ℤ) | puCut T (mob δ τ) ≠ 0}, which is finite by `hasFiniteSupport_puCut_mob T τ` (no Γ, no FiniteIndex). If smoothedFundamental Γ T (γ•τ) ≠ 0, then by the contrapositive of `finsum_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero` (additive form of `finprod_eq_one_of_forall_eq_one`) some coset q has puCut T (mob q.out (γ•τ)) ≠ 0. By `coe_smul` and `mob_mob` this equals puCut T (mob (q.out * γ) τ), so δ := q.out*γ ∈ S. Since γ ∈ Γ, (q.out)⁻¹δ = γ ∈ Γ, so ⟦δ⟧ = q (left cosets) and γ = (⟦δ⟧.out)⁻¹ * δ. Hence the support lies in the image of the finite set S under δ ↦ (⟦δ⟧.out)⁻¹δ and is finite. Degenerate cases: infinite index only shrinks the support; when Γ is trivial the support still injects into S.
